overall: Los Angeles reached its daily peak temperature of 73.4°F at approximately 15:00 ET (noon local PT), and has been cooling steadily since — now sitting at 69.8°F with a velocity of -1.8°F/hr as of 19:49 ET. The day ran notably warmer than expected, exceeding both the NWS point forecast of 71°F and all NWP model guidance. With temperatures on a clear downward trajectory well into the afternoon, the daily maximum almost certainly has been set.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models undershot the observed high: ECMWF came in at 71.2°F, HRRR at 71.0°F, and NBM well below at 67.2°F, yet the running max already stands at 73.4°F — 2 to 6°F above their projections. The model consensus on peak timing (mean 17.3h ET) is later than the observed peak at 15:00 ET, suggesting models also missed the timing of the warmth. The INTRADAY model's anomalously high probabilities for the 84–85°F bucket appear to be a spurious artifact, as hourly observations clearly contradict any such warming scenario; the ensemble signals correctly flag abort/no-trade.
max_temp_prediction: With the running maximum confirmed at 73.4°F and temperatures cooling at -1.8°F/hr nearly five hours past the observed peak, the daily TMAX is effectively locked in at 73.4°F. The META model's leading buckets of 74–75°F (38.3%) and 72–73°F (22.9%) bracket this observation well, with 73.4°F sitting solidly in the 72–73°F range. Confidence is high — there is no meaningful chance of additional warming tonight given the clear diurnal cooling trend and a forecast overnight low of 61°F.
